page0.text:
I broke my promise to her, so anything I say is just an excuse.
I need to do whatever I can to make it up to Illya, but I don't know what would make her happy.
Then...why don't you act like a Master and use your Command Spells to make your wish come true?

page1.text: "Why are you all quiet? That face won't fool me. If you're not going to apologize, then I won't either. If you don't like me, then I'll—"

page2.text:
"All right. Illya, I'm your Servant. To make it up to you for breaking our promise, why don't I be your Servant just this once?"
"...turn you into a puppet—wait, my Servant!?"

page3.text: "That's right. It's too late to hang out today. So, I'll do whatever you ask, just once. That should make you feel a little better, right?"

page4.text:
".........
No, you're lying! You didn't come to the park. Anyone can break a verbal promise, so I don't believe you!"

page5.text: "I know. So I'll treat it like a Command Spell to prove it to you. I'll make a promise I can't break, just this once. Will you trust me then?"

page6.text: "T-trust you... But I don't have any Command Spells that work on you..."

page7.text:
"Yeah. But I swear I'll keep my word. It isn't a real contract and the Command Spell will not actually be used, but I'll act like you cast one on me.
You and I are both Masters. I can swear on my own crest that I won't break a promise we treat as a Command Spell."

page8.text:
I stand up straight and swear an oath to Illya.
The silver-haired girl takes a quiet breath.
"...You'll really do anything I say?"
She looks at me uneasily.

page9.text:
"Of course. It's a Command Spell, you know. I'll do whatever's within my power to obey."
I return her anxious gaze with a heartfelt smile.

page10.text:
"..."
A long silence passes between us.
Illya looks away and clutches her hands together.

page11.text:
"...All right. Then...take me..."
"Huh?"
Did I hear her correctly?
I was expecting an order worthy of a Command Spell, but it's a much smaller wish than that.

page12.text: "Illya...? Wait, I said a Command Spell. I'll do absolutely anything you say. Are you sure that's what you want?"

page13.text:
"..."
"You could ask for something else. That's way too easy. C'mon, don't hold back on my account. Ask me to—"
"I'm not holding back! You lied! You said you would do anything!"

page14.text:
"Uh, yeah, I will! But are you sure, Illya? I mean, that's too..."
Something I'd do for you anytime you asked, no Command Spell needed.

page15.text:
"...No, it isn't. It's something I've always wanted. And it's what I want most from you right now."
Blushing furiously, Illya trembles as if anticipating rejection.

page16.text:
"...Illya."
I shouldn't keep doubting her courage.
It's her number one wish, even if it sounds simple.
Right now, I just need to serve Illya the best I can, as her knight.

page17.text:
"All right. Sorry for the stupid question.
Let's go, Illya. The shopping district isn't big, but it'll be fun to walk around."

page18.text:
I feel my face get hot at the way I phrased it.
I know I'm blushing red.
Without hiding it, I give Illya my hand.

page19.text:
Her wish is a trivial one:
"Take me shopping."
Nothing special at all.
Illya wants to do something completely normal, that I could help her with as many times as she wants.

page20.text:
...I can't imagine what it must mean to her.
I just do as she asks and walk around the shopping district with her. Not as enemies or allies, not as Masters, but as brother and sister.
She stares with wonder at shops I know well and sights I'm sick of seeing.

page21.text:
Her excitement is so infectious that I have fun just watching her.
She walks through the street with a sunny, carefree smile.
I wish I could make this moment last forever for her.

page22.text:
But sadly, I start to understand.
Her smile doesn't crack for a second. She dances through the street.
This isn't happiness.
She's smiling desperately, because she's sad. Because she doesn't want to wake up from this dream.

page23.text:
"Over here, Shirou! Your coffee's going to get cold!"
Illya runs toward the park with the two drinks she bought. Maybe she hasn't seen hot canned beverages before.

page24.text:
I wish this day could go on. I want to tell her she doesn't have to keep doing this. But, everything must come to an end.
Miyama's shopping district is small.
No matter how slowly we go, we can see it all in an hour.

page25.text:
"And here we are! This is our last stop, Shirou.
You can rest now. Thanks for working so hard today."

page26.text:
In front of the bench, Illya twirls to face me.
She beckons me to sit and rest, so I do.

page27.text:
And yet...
Illya doesn't sit, even though she invited me to.

page28.text:
"Illya? Aren't you going to sit down?"
"Mm-hm. Here's your drink, Shirou. Yours is coffee, and mine is shiruko."

page29.text:
Illya takes only one can out of her pocket and hands it to me.
She keeps the other can in her coat pocket. It's the only thing she badgered me into buying today.

page30.text:
"I'm surprised you know what shiruko is, Illya. I bet they don't have red bean drinks overseas."
"Yeah. It's my first time seeing it. A long time ago, someone told me it's really sweet, so I shouldn't drink it."

page31.text:
Illya grins at me and does a little step and twirl.
She makes her way to the center of the park, practically dancing as she goes.

page32.text:
"Illya...?"
"The Command Spell is over now. It wasn't a long time, but thanks, Shirou."
There isn't a hint of gloom in her voice.
She gives me a smile free of any regrets, declaring an abrupt end to the dream.

page33.text: "Wha—what are you thanking me for? It hasn't even been an hour. If you're tired of this place, we can go see the city. There's a lot more—"

page34.text:
"It's okay. This is our last stop. It's been fun, but shopping is over. Once the sun sets soon, we'll be back to our old relationship.
We'll both be Masters; I'll try to kill you, while you defend yourself. I've understood that since before we met."

page35.text:
What am I supposed to say to that determined smile?
Illya wants a normal life more than I ever would, and yet she casts it aside more easily than I ever could.

page36.text:
"I see. So once we leave this park..."
"We'll be enemies again. The next time we meet at night, we'll continue what we started last time.
So if you don't want me to kill you, then you'll have to kill me first, Shirou."

page37.text:
My breath catches in my throat, and I look up at the sky.
The sky is an overcast gray.
Heavy clouds cover the town, bringing an end to the happy times.
I wish they could last forever, but I knew this moment would come once I realized that would only be harder on Illya.

page38.text:
She said that this is our last stop.
The end of the line.
Here, where there's nowhere else to go and no way back, Illya keeps smiling innocently.

page39.text:
"Wow! Look Shirou, snow!"
Her cheerful voice captures my attention.
When I look back at the park, I'm greeted by a distant scene.

page40.text:
For a second, I think I'm seeing things.
It's not the falling snow that surprises me, but the unreal sight of Illya dancing.

page41.text:
...
The snow is only temporary.
I can tell it's just a bit of powder snow that will stop soon.

page42.text:
But under it, in this uncertain winter, the area around Illya is so white.
The silver-haired girl frolics in the fleeting frost, as if loved by winter itself.

page43.text:
"Aha! The snow here is so warm. This is my first time seeing such normal snowfall."
Illya twirls and twirls, overjoyed.

page44.text:
"You're awfully upbeat. Do you like snow, Illya?"
"Yeah. I don't like the cold, but I like snow itself. It's gentle and reminds me of my mother. Also, she told me my white hair was pretty."

page45.text:
Her smile is so merry.
Intuitively, I know who said that to her.

page46.text: "The snow here is so pretty. So it snows properly in the land where Kiritsugu lived, huh?"

page47.text:
That carefree smile isn't for me.
...Illyasviel von Einzbern.
The pale girl who came here to kill my father.
She came here looking for Kiritsugu, and she's trying to kill me.
...I've long since realized the true reason why.

page48.text:
He betrayed the Einzberns.
Then, he threw away his entire life to come live here.
From the perspective of Kiritsugu's son, she's a child who's been chasing after a man who has nothing to do with her.
Until I became a Master, I had no idea what he gave up.

page49.text:
The snow seems to hide Illya as she dances.
The girl from a faraway country bids me farewell with a smile.

page50.text: "Bye, Shirou. If I see you walking around alone again, I'll play with you!"

page51.text: Smiling innocently, the pale girl disappears from the park.
